Make the void proportion large enough to read as a court rather than a superficial cut.
Open the void toward the program access side to support an active street threshold.
Move the cantilever closer to the frontage so the ground plane gains a clearer undercut/entry seam.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the shallow corner notch into a more legible carved void so the mass reads as a public court/entry condition rather than a small cut.
Align the opening to the program-defined access side so the frontage can become the dominant public threshold.
Increase the notch depth so the void becomes spatially readable in plan and section.
Widen the opening to strengthen public access and avoid a token incision.
Keep the subtraction grounded and usable rather than a full-height void that would erase the primary mass.
Shift the cantilever earlier so the lifted portion better frames the public threshold and produces a clearer ground response.

rationale: The mass is compact and not obviously incoherent across views, but it does not yet support the neighborhood-living brief strongly enough. The dominant form reads as a small stepped block with a shallow notch rather than a clear public-facing ground response. The blue access edge is not convincingly answered by an open court, seam, or undercut; instead the mass feels largely sealed and semantically neutral at the frontage. The silhouette has some continuity, but the steps feel more like arbitrary tiering than a capacity-bearing inhabited section. Reference resonance exists in the general courtyard/terrace language, but the candidate is missing the stronger void-publicness and active threshold logic that those precedents demonstrate. Because the program contract requires an active ground edge and a clear public void or terrace, the current mass fails program_fit_hard_pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion/cultural than neighborhood-living; the candidate lacks this level of void legibility and bridge-to-court clarity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a central carved void and an upper bridge can support a compact neighborhood/public program.
